column1: {{c1::Photosynthesis}} converts light energy into chemical energy stored in {{c2::sugars}}.
column2:
Carried out by plants, algae and cyanobacteria.

Source: [S1 ¶1]

column1: Organisms that make their own food from inorganic molecules are called {{c1::autotrophs (producers)}}.
The fluid inside a chloroplast is the {{c1::stroma}}; the flattened membrane sacs inside it are {{c2::thylakoids}}, stacked into {{c3::grana}}.
At the end of the electron transport chain, electrons reduce {{c1::NADP⁺}} to {{c2::NADPH}}.
Splitting water to replace chlorophyll's lost electrons is called {{c1::photolysis}}.
In carbon fixation, the enzyme {{c1::Rubisco}} attaches CO₂ to the five-carbon sugar {{c2::RuBP}}.
For every {{c1::three}} molecules of CO₂ fixed, one G3P leaves the Calvin cycle.
A {{c1::limiting factor}} is whichever of light intensity, CO₂ concentration and temperature is in shortest supply.
column2:
Raising the other two doesn't increase the rate until it's increased.
